newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares ended firm on Monday after bullion rose three dollars to around $343 an ounce, dealers said.
"We saw a bit of a kick in the gold price and players responding almost with disbelief, not knowing how to handle this rise," a dealer said.
A softer rand also helped boost gold shares, dealers said.
They added that if bullion held these gains or advanced slightly further, gold shares would tick up on Tuesday.

Industrials were also firm on positive sentiment in the market due to a better-than-expected gold and foreign exchange reserves number last Friday and talk that funds from the 30 percent stake sale of state telecommunications utility Telkom may come through this month.
However dealers said further gains in the market were hampered by the absence of UK players who were enjoying an Early May public holiday.

"It was a firm day. It is a pity that London is closed otherwise the market would have been stronger. The market needed support from world markets," Johan Marais, director at Societe General Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
The gold index ended up 24.1 points at 1,205.7 points, lifting the index from the four year lows it has been plumbing in the last few sessions.
The industrial index gained 24.9 points to 8,563.4 points and the all-share index was 41.4 points stronger at 7,190.4 points.
Interest in the gold sector selected Kloof which was 90 cents stronger at 30.90 rand, Freegold which was up 140 cents to 31.50 rand and Dries added 110 cents to 38.50 rand.

The financial sector also saw some interest, rising 85.2 points to a record 9,078.9 points. It was helped, in part, by gains in Nedcor of 3.05 percent to 93 rand and Stanbic rising 2.93 percent to 211 rand.
Foreign trade in Foodcorp saw volumes traded rise to nearly 28 million rand worth. The share gained 50 cents to new year high of 33.10 rand.

Unihold shares were up on heavy volume after it issued a cautionary announcement in the morning. The share picked up 20 cents, or 5.71 percent, to 370 cents on volume of over 1.9 million shares valued at over seven million rand.

Dealers said volumes trade on Monday were on the light side with only 566 million rand worth of shares traded. The market was seen looking to Wall Street and the bullion price for direction on Tuesday.
Near-dated gold share futures also saw some interest on a better bullion price. Industrial contracts ended firm on Friday's stronger Wall Street. Volumes were fair, dealers said.
The June all-share contract was at 6,695/704 from 6,673, industrial contracts was at 8,416/24 from 8,385 and the gold contract was little changed at 847/53 from 845.
